title: Bronze / Silver / Gold: define the contracts
summary: Theory / Modern Data Stack & Governance / Layered architecture / Quality and ownership

children.text: Explain a medallion data architecture and what belongs in Bronze, Silver and Gold.

items: Keep replayable inputs and ingestion metadata in Bronze.
Define keys, types, quality rules and deduplication in Silver.
Publish business measures and usable contracts in Gold.
Explain lineage, access and ownership across layers.

children.text: Bronze retains source-like data for replay. Silver validates and standardizes data at a documented grain. Gold exposes consumer-oriented products such as customer revenue aggregates. These are logical quality contracts, not a requirement to copy every dataset three times.

  A[Source systems] --> B[Bronze: source-like data]
  B --> C[Silver: validated records]
  C --> D[Gold: business products]

children.title: Watch for this
children.text: Calling a table Gold does not validate its metric definition. Preserve raw inputs and specify who owns quality failures.

items: Where would you quarantine invalid records and how would you reprocess them?
Place transformations according to data quality and consumer needs.
